description: Adversarial review lenses consumed by midas-code-review. A lens is one question asked of a diff. Lenses are selected per change class, never all at once: selection above three lenses is permitted only when multiple change classes each demand distinct lenses, and the selection records why.

lenses.name: Edge-Case Hunter
lenses.question: What input, state, or timing did the author not think about, and what does the code do when it arrives?
redFlags: Boundary values (zero, empty, max, negative) untested
Error paths that assume the happy path already succeeded
Concurrency or reentry unconsidered on shared state
Unicode, locale, or timezone assumptions baked into parsing
Silent fallbacks that hide the unexpected case instead of surfacing it
lenses.evidenceRequired: A named list of boundary and failure cases with the test or trace proving each is handled — or an explicit record that it is not.

lenses.name: Hostile-User Lens
lenses.question: If this change shipped to a hostile user today, what is the worst they could do with it?
redFlags: Input reaching a sink (query, shell, path, URL) without validation
Authorization checked client-side only, or not per-object
Secrets or tokens logged, committed, or echoed in errors
New dependency or network surface added without review
Error messages leaking internal structure to callers
lenses.evidenceRequired: The trust boundary named, the inputs crossing it enumerated, and the check (test or code path) shown for each crossing.

lenses.name: Contract Reader
lenses.question: Does the change do exactly what the governing spec or contract says — no more, no less?
redFlags: Behavior present that no requirement asked for
A requirement silently narrowed or reinterpreted to fit the code
Docs or schema drifting from the implemented behavior
Contract fields renamed or repurposed without a version bump
lenses.evidenceRequired: The governing spec quoted next to the diff hunk that satisfies it, requirement by requirement.

lenses.name: What-Broke Lens
lenses.question: What that worked before this change could stop working because of it?
redFlags: Shared helper modified with call sites unchecked
A test deleted or loosened to make the suite pass
Default value or ordering changed in passing
Migration shipped without a rollback path
lenses.evidenceRequired: The full pre-existing suite run green on the change, plus a usage search for every modified shared surface.

lenses.name: Receipt Auditor
lenses.question: Is every claim this change makes or enables — in code, copy, or docs — backed by a receipt?
redFlags: Metrics or counts stated without a source
Intent worded as live capability
A 'verified' label with no quoted command output behind it
Pricing or entitlement copy diverging from the enforced behavior
lenses.evidenceRequired: Each user-visible or reviewer-visible claim mapped to its evidence: the command, output, or enforced code path that makes it true.

lenses.name: Hot-Path Accountant
lenses.question: Where does this change spend time or memory that it did not before, and at what scale does that hurt?
redFlags: Work moved inside a loop or render path
Unbounded collection growth, or a cache without eviction
N+1 I/O introduced where one batch call would do
Blocking call added on a hot path
lenses.evidenceRequired: A measurement — timing, profile, or complexity argument with realistic input sizes — for the affected path, before and after.
